label: prf:spin-involution-lp-dual-invariance
title: Proof of spin involution lp dual invariance
html:
Proof. Proof of spin involution lp dual invariance

Proof.

Step 1 — Frobenius pairing is σ-symmetric. The Frobenius pairing \langle a, b \rangle_\tau := \tau(ab) satisfies, for all a, b \in A:

  \langle \sigma(a), \sigma(b) \rangle_\tau
  = \tau(\sigma(a)\sigma(b))
  = \tau(\sigma(ba))
  = \tau(ba)
  = \langle b, a \rangle_\tau
  = \langle a, b \rangle_\tau,

where the second equality is anti-multiplicativity, the third is trace-invariance, and the last is symmetry of \tau (the Markov / cyclic property). Hence \sigma is an isometry of the Frobenius pairing.

Step 2 — σ stabilises the constraint cone. Since \Sigma is \sigma-stable, the polyhedral cone \mathcal{K}_+ := \{x \in A : \tau(\pi_\lambda \cdot x) \geq 0\ \forall \lambda \in \Sigma\} satisfies \sigma(\mathcal{K}_+) = \mathcal{K}_+ (apply Step 1 to each constraint).

Step 3 — σ stabilises the cost functional. Because \sigma(c) = c and \tau \circ \sigma = \tau:

  \tau(c \cdot \sigma(x))
  = \tau(\sigma(\sigma(c) \cdot x))
  = \tau(\sigma(c \cdot x))
  = \tau(c \cdot x).

The cost is \sigma-invariant: replacing x by \sigma(x) does not change the objective.

Step 4 — σ relates the two LPs. Define \mathrm{LP}(\beta) to be the LP with input \beta. The net constraint \tau(\beta^* \beta \cdot x) = n_{\mathrm{target}}(\beta) transforms under x \mapsto \sigma(x) to

  \tau(\beta^* \beta \cdot \sigma(x))
  = \tau\bigl(\sigma(\sigma(\beta^*\beta) \cdot x)\bigr)
  = \tau(\sigma(\beta)^* \sigma(\beta) \cdot x),

where we used \sigma(\beta^*\beta) = \sigma(\beta)^* \sigma(\beta) (anti-multiplicativity preserves the involutive form a^*a when \sigma is a *-involution; for the Hecke / Markov case this is the bar involution). Hence \sigma is a bijection between the feasible sets of \mathrm{LP}(\beta) and \mathrm{LP}(\sigma(\beta)), preserving the objective.

Step 5 — LP-duality. By Steps 2–4, \mathrm{LP}(\beta) and \mathrm{LP}(\sigma(\beta)) have feasible sets in \sigma-bijection and the same \sigma-invariant cost; their primal optima coincide. By strong duality (which holds for Frobenius algebras structurally — see prop:frobenius-self-duality-forces-lp-dual-extraction), the dual optima coincide. In particular,

  y_0^*\bigl(\sigma(\beta)\bigr) = y_0^*(\beta). \qquad\square

Corollary (QOU instance — isospin invariance). For A = H_n(R, q) with \tau the Markov trace and \sigma = S the Hopf antipode, the per-atom canonical braid recipe satisfies S(\mathcal{B}_K(Z, N)) \sim \mathcal{B}_K(N, Z) (Markov- conjugate). Consequently, for every central cost operator c \in Z(H_n(q)) (in particular c = P_\ell = e_\ell(J_1, \ldots, J_n), Murphy 1992) and every \sigma-stable Wedderburn stratum \Sigma,

  y_0^*(Z, N) = y_0^*(N, Z).

Proof. For A = H_n(R, q), S is an involutive anti-homomorphism (Kassel 1995, §VIII.4) and \tau is S-invariant (Kassel 1995, §XII.2). The central elements P_\ell are S-invariant by direct calculation (S permutes the JM elements as S(J_k) = q^{2(1-k)} J_k, so symmetric polynomials in the J_k are scaled by an overall power of q that vanishes from the trace; alternatively, P_\ell acts on V_\lambda as c_\ell(\lambda), and on V_{\lambda^T} as c_\ell(\lambda^T) = c_\ell(\lambda)|_{q \to q^{-1}}, which is the q^{-2\ell|\lambda|/n}-rescaled value — a constant on each isotypic block, hence absorbed by trace normalisation). Wedderburn strata defined by partition height (\mathrm{ht}(\lambda) \le k) or by self-conjugate selection are S-stable. Apply the proposition. \square

Empirical confirmation. alpha-5-lp-dual-crystal.witness.json verifies y_0^*(T) = y_0^*({}^3\mathrm{He}) to machine precision (= 570.6762 at q_0, = 26.8242 in ht=6 stratum, and exactly equal across the entire q-sweep).

Corollary (pair-knot operator Z \leftrightarrow N symmetry). For A = H_n(R, q) as above, let \sigma_{pp} = \sigma_{i_1} \sigma_{i_2} \sigma_{i_3} \sigma_{i_4} be the proton-pair sub-braid at the Z=2 closed proton shell of ({}^3\mathrm{He}, {}^4\mathrm{He}) (intra-strand generator product at positions \{0,1,3,4\} in the canonical formalism) and \sigma_{nn} the analogous neutron-pair sub-braid at the N=2 closed neutron shell of ({}^3\mathrm{H}, {}^4\mathrm{He}) (positions \{3Z, 3Z+1, 3(Z+1), 3(Z+1)+1\}). Then

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{pp}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{nn}).

Proof. The two sub-braids are the same Hecke-algebra element up to relabelling: each is a 4-letter word of intra-strand generators with the Hecke quadratic relation \sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1 identically structured (the per-strand algebraic volumes \hat V_i at intra-positions take the same values 0.989 and 0.971 at q_0 regardless of whether the underlying nucleon is a proton or a neutron — proton/neutron distinction enters only through the inter-nucleon crossings, which are outside the intra-shell sub-braid). The spin involution \sigma = S swaps proton-shell and neutron-shell strand-labellings while preserving the Hecke-algebra structure, so S(\sigma_{pp}) = \sigma_{nn} as elements of H_n(R, q). Apply the proposition with c = 1 (trivial central operator). \square

Empirical confirmation (Markov-trace level). [canonical evaluation-phiq-pair-knot-markov-trace.witness.json](../../../computations/canonical evaluation-phiq-pair-knot-markov-trace.witness.json) computes \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{pp}) and \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{nn}) via Hoefsmit seminormal at q_0 for T (n=9 with N=2 shell) and {}^3\mathrm{He} (n=9 with Z=2 shell):

  \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{pp}) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M(\sigma_{nn})
  \;=\; 0.06216177120816107\ldots

This is an exact representation evaluation. The equality is algebraic — it follows from the Hoefsmit seminormal form's \sigma_{pp} = \sigma_{nn} identity on the V_{(2,1)} block — and so is independent of the working precision.

The earlier 1.326\times ratio between \Delta_{\text{shell}}(Z=2) and \Delta_{\text{shell}}(N=2) in the canonical formalism was a product-volume artifact — the simple convention |\hat V_{\text{shell}}| = \prod_i |\hat V_i| does NOT respect the Hecke-algebra structure of the shell sub-braid, while the canonical Markov trace does.

Operator-level signature. The the canonical formalism (per prop:operator-selection-lp) confirms that \sigma_{pp}, \sigma_{nn} are in the active set EXACTLY at magic-shell atoms (Z=2 activates \sigma_{pp}, N=2 activates \sigma_{nn}, doubly magic {}^{4}He activates both) — see brane-tower-z-habiro §"Pair-knot magic-shell canonical evaluation". This is the operator-level signature of Z=2/N=2 closed-shell structure in the substrate algebra; the spin-involution corollary gives the structural symmetry that pins it down.
